name: Novah
beneficiaries_note: Our build: NOVAH's radio drama aired in Rwanda only in 2025.
summary: NOVAH makes Twubakane, a radio drama about a Rwandan couple that learns to decide together, to prevent violence against women by their partners. In 2025 it spent $173,600: its first six-episode season aired on a regional station in northern Rwanda and about 27,000 adults followed it, and the money also made a second season for a 2026 trial. With partner violence falling by a judged quarter among couples who listen (a trial of similar videos in Uganda, and NOVAH's own small pilot) and each year of violence costing about {{row:dalys_per_ipv_year}} healthy years by the Global Burden of Disease's count, it comes to about {{result}} years of healthy life per $1,000. The biggest uncertainties are whether the drama reduces violence at all and how much harm a year of violence averted spares; until NOVAH's own trial reports, the effect is discounted for missing data.

resources.title: Green, Wilke and Cooper (2020), Countering Violence Against Women by Encouraging Disclosure: A Mass Media Experiment in Rural Uganda, Comparative Political Studies 53(14): 2283-2320 (open copy hosted by IPA)
Sardinha et al. (2022), Global, regional, and national prevalence estimates of physical or sexual, or both, intimate partner violence against women in 2018, The Lancet
Persistent burden and health inequalities of disease in women of childbearing age attributable to Intimate Partner Violence, 1990-2021, Frontiers in Psychiatry 2025

sections.title: Cost
sections.explainer: What the modelled program cost in the year the outcomes below are counted for, including its share of overhead. From audited financial statements or the annual report.

sections.title: Reach
sections.explainer: How many people, animals or meals the spending reached in the same year, as the charity reports it.

sections.title: Effect per unit
sections.explainer: What the intervention does for each unit reached, from the best available studies, before any adjustment.

sections.title: Adjustments
sections.explainer: Discounts for weaker evidence, what would have happened anyway, credit shared with others, and delivery falling short. All multiply the outcome.

sections.title: Other outcomes, in this model's unit
sections.explainer: charityevals' standard step for outcomes in more than one unit (docs/normalization.md 2.6): each outcome is counted in its own unit (units of value for income and deaths, WELLBYs for life satisfaction, tonnes of CO₂e, chicken pain days) and put into this model's unit by its unit's conversion over this unit's, which the headline's conversion cancels. So each moves only with its own sliders, exactly as in a model of its own unit. The rows are fixed; don't edit them.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.explainer: The outcome in the family's shared unit, per dollar.

sections.title: Your dollar's share
sections.explainer: Staff who earn less than they could elsewhere pay part of the cost in kind. With credit by share of resources, your dollar is credited with its share of the full cost only.

rows.label: NOVAH's spending in 2025, both accounts (its one programme, the Twubakane radio drama)
rows.explainer: Everything NOVAH spent in calendar 2025, across the Dutch foundation and its US fiscal sponsor (Players Philanthropy Fund), from its own transaction records in US dollars: the two co-directors and international subcontractors ($80,013), Season 1's airing and evaluations ($15,530), Season 2's production and evaluation and the trial's preparation ($65,478), events ($5,445) and administration ($7,134). NOVAH has one programme, so all of it is counted; 2025's money also made Season 2, which aired in 2026, as 2024's made Season 1, which aired in 2025 (Convention 3: one year's delivery against one year's cost). The Dutch accounts (compiled, not audited) cover only the foundation's share, EUR 94,175 over September 2024 to December 2025.

rows.label: Total expenses, 2025 (both accounts)
rows.explainer: The same total: the management accounts don't split management and fundraising from the programme.

rows.label: Programme expenses (all programmes), 2025
rows.explainer: NOVAH has one programme and its accounts don't split overhead out, so this equals the spending modelled.

rows.label: Overhead multiplier (total ÷ program expenses)
rows.explainer: Spreads management and fundraising over programs in proportion to their cost, as GiveWell and ACE do.

rows.label: Cost of the programme, including overhead
rows.explainer: All of NOVAH's 2025 spending.

rows.label: Adults who actively listened to Season 1 on RC Musanze (February 2025)

source.title: NOVAH, Annual Activity Report 2024-2025
source.quote: A post-broadcast quantitative survey of 500 people found approximately 27,000 active listeners in the coverage area (representing 7% of the total adult population in the catchment area).

rows.explainer: NOVAH's own survey of 500 adults a week after the six 20-minute episodes aired on RC Musanze, the national broadcaster's station in northern Rwanda: 7% of the 375,000 adults in its coverage area could answer a question about the story (four times as many said they had listened but couldn't). 31 of the 500 were active listeners (the reported 7% counts adult respondents only), so the range is the binomial 95% interval of a share near 6-7% from about 500 people, 4.4% to 8.7% of 375,000 adults; no independent count exists.

rows.label: Share of active listeners who are married or in a union

source.title: NOVAH, Twubakane's evaluation (season 1)
source.quote: Among those who actively listened and were married (n=26), more than 90% said that their relationship has changed since listening to the show

rows.explainer: 26 of the survey's 31 active listeners were married, 84%; the range is the binomial 95% interval of so small a sample.

rows.label: Married active listeners per couple reached
rows.explainer: Both spouses heard it in many couples: 80% of active listeners listened with their spouse or family, and 60% were women (evaluation, p. 9). If every couple reached had one listener this would be 1, if both always listened 2. Our judgment 1.5, 1.2 to 1.9.

rows.label: Couples with at least one active listener
rows.explainer: About {{row:broadcast_couples}} couples in the station's area.

rows.label: Couples in the intervention villages of the 2025 pilot study

source.title: NOVAH, Annual Activity Report 2024-2025
source.quote: In 2025, NOVAH conducted a baseline-endline pilot study with 200 couples (140 in intervention villages, 60 in control villages) in Rwanda's Eastern Province

rows.explainer: Couples in Eastern Province who listened to Season 1 for the pilot study in mid-2025, outside the broadcast's area.

rows.label: Couples reached in 2025 (the woman in each is the unit counted)
rows.explainer: The unit the effect below applies to: a woman in a couple where Season 1 was heard. Season 2 aired in 2026, against 2026's spending, and isn't counted here.

rows.label: Cost per couple reached
rows.explainer: About {{row:cost_per_person}} per couple: one regional season's audience against a year that also paid for the next season and a trial's preparation.

rows.label: Years the drama's effect on violence lasts
rows.explainer: The Uganda trial measured violence over the six months up to its survey eight months after the screenings and still found the effect; NOVAH's pilot measured six weeks after listening. Nothing measured later. Our judgment one year, 0.4 (it fades within months) to 2 (couples keep the habits).

rows.label: Share of married women suffering physical or sexual partner violence in a year, without the drama
rows.explainer: Rwanda's national figure from the 2019-20 DHS, 23.6%: ever-married women, violence by their current or most recent partner. The women reached are in current couples, whose violence is somewhat less common (ever-violence 35.8% among the currently married against 40.3% of all ever-married), but in the North, where the broadcast was, it is more common (43.4% ever; Table 16.10.1); the two roughly offset. NOVAH's pilot implies about 15% in its villages (6 points = 40%), over a shorter recall.

rows.label: Relative fall in partner violence among women in couples with an active listener, at the dose they got

source.title: Green, Wilke and Cooper (2020), Countering Violence Against Women by Encouraging Disclosure: A Mass Media Experiment in Rural Uganda, Comparative Political Studies 53(14): 2283-2320 (open copy hosted by IPA)
source.page: Table 4, column 5 (individual level, all women), p. 2307

rows.explainer: Our judgment for the broadcast audience as it listened (anyone who heard some of the season, often one spouse alone), from three anchors, none a published trial of this drama. The Uganda trial of short anti-violence videos at village screenings: women reporting any violence in their household over six months fell 4.9 points from 21% (SE 2.2), a quarter, among all women in treatment villages, and 13.1 points (SE 4.9), about 60%, among women who attended. NOVAH's 2025 pilot of Season 1 with 200 couples (not randomised, difference in differences, six weeks after): 6 points, 40%, published without a confidence interval and called underpowered by NOVAH. Its 2026 trial of Season 2 has no published result. The active listeners sit between Uganda's all women (most attended no screening) and its attenders, and below the pilot's couples who heard the whole season: 25%, 5% to 50%.

rows.label: Share of women aged 15-49 ever partnered, Eastern sub-Saharan Africa
rows.explainer: To turn the region's prevalence among ever-partnered women into a share of all its women, as the GBD rates below are. Rwanda marries late: 59.6% of its women 15-49 have ever married (DHS 2019-20, Table 4.1), the low end; in the region's large countries (Ethiopia, Tanzania, Uganda, Kenya, Mozambique) roughly a quarter to a third of women 15-49 have never married, and 'ever-partnered' is wider than ever married. Our judgment 72%, 60% to 82%.

rows.label: Share of women aged 15-49 suffering partner violence in a year, Eastern sub-Saharan Africa
rows.explainer: The region's past-year prevalence among ever-partnered women times the share ever partnered, so that the GBD rates per woman below become rates per woman suffering violence that year.

rows.label: Rwanda's health burden per year of partner violence against its region's
rows.explainer: The GBD rates are the region's, and about two thirds of its burden is years of life lost, mostly to HIV. Rwanda's adult HIV prevalence is about 2.5-3% against about 3.5% for the region weighted by population (UNAIDS country estimates), with high treatment coverage, so fewer of its infections end in death; the depression, anxiety and injuries carry over. Our judgment 75% of the region's burden, deaths and illness alike, 55% to 100%.

rows.label: Healthy years lost per woman-year of partner violence (GBD, deaths included)
rows.explainer: GBD 2021's DALYs from partner violence per woman aged 15-49 in Rwanda's region, over the share suffering it in a year, scaled to Rwanda: about {{row:dalys_per_ipv_year}}. In a steady state each year's burden is what that year's violence goes on to cause.

rows.label: Deaths per woman-year of partner violence (GBD)
rows.explainer: The same for deaths, mostly HIV and homicide: about {{row:deaths_per_ipv_year}}.

rows.label: Years GBD counts as lost for each attributable death (to take deaths out of its DALYs)
rows.explainer: To take the deaths out of the DALYs (deaths are valued by age below, as in every model): GBD counts a death's years against its reference life table, about 58 years left at 30 and about 40 at 45; partner-violence deaths among women 15-49 come mostly between 25 and 45. Our judgment 50, 40 to 58.

rows.label: Share of that burden a year of violence averted removes
rows.explainer: Health harm only (the fear and pain of the violence itself are counted once, in other_unmodelled_share). GBD attributes its burden to ever having suffered violence. If harm followed each year of violence, a year averted would remove a full year's share (1); if only ever being exposed mattered, it would remove little for a woman already abused. HIV through a violent partner accrues with each year of exposure, and longitudinal studies find recent violence followed by new depressive symptoms (Devries et al. 2013, PLoS Medicine, systematic review), both nearer 1; some depression and anxiety persist from past violence whatever happens next year. Our judgment 0.75, 0.4 to 1.

rows.label: Years from the violence to the middle of its health harms
rows.explainer: Depression and anxiety follow within months; HIV deaths come years later. Our judgment 3 years, 1 to 8.

rows.label: Discount for the years until the violence's health harms come
rows.explainer: Discounted at the shared rate from the middle of the harms.

rows.label: Deaths a year caused by partner violence, per woman reached
rows.explainer: Women suffering violence in a year times the deaths a year of it causes, discounted to when they come.

rows.label: Share of violence (and the deaths it causes) the drama prevents
rows.explainer: The relative fall in violence above, before adjustments.

rows.label: Other deaths averted per death averted
rows.explainer: 0: GBD's attributable deaths already include every cause it links to partner violence.

rows.label: Deaths averted per person reached (before adjustments)
rows.explainer: Direct and indirect deaths over the years of protection. If the intervention protects several age groups with different risks, replace this formula with one row per group and sum them here; check the result against the all-cause trial result per person-year, scaled to today's mortality.

rows.label: Share of deaths averted under age 5
rows.explainer: 0: the deaths counted are of women 15-49.

rows.label: Share aged 5-14 of the deaths averted
rows.explainer: 0: the deaths counted are of women 15-49.

rows.label: Share aged 15-49 of the deaths averted over 15
rows.explainer: All: GBD's rate here counts deaths of women 15-49.

rows.label: Woman-years of partner violence averted per couple reached (before adjustments)
rows.explainer: 23.6% times the relative fall times the years it lasts. For reading and for the illness below.

rows.label: Healthy years lost to illness per woman-year of violence (deaths taken out), discounted
rows.formula: max(0, dalys_per_ipv_year - deaths_per_ipv_year * gbd_yll_per_death) * burden_per_year_adj * harm_discount
rows.explainer: GBD's DALYs less the deaths' years of life lost: the years lived with depression, anxiety, HIV and injuries, about {{row:illness_dalys_per_ipv_year}}.

rows.label: Illness averted as a share of the deaths' value
rows.explainer: 0: illness is counted once, in DALYs (dalys_illness_averted_per_person).

rows.label: Stillbirths averted per couple reached
rows.explainer: 0: GBD's burden of partner violence counts no stillbirths; harms in pregnancy are in the unmodelled share.

rows.label: Later-life income gain per couple reached, ln(consumption) per year
rows.explainer: 0: no study measured income; women's lost work is in the unmodelled share.

rows.label: Years until the income gain starts
rows.explainer: Unused (no income gain is modelled); the template's shared figure is kept so the row means the same in every model.

rows.label: Years the long-term income gain lasts
rows.explainer: The site's one figure for how long a long-term income gain lasts (GiveWell's working years, 40), read by every model that counts one (INV-13).

rows.label: Later-life income gain per person reached, present value
rows.explainer: Discounted at the shared rate, the wait included, so the result moves with it. Never type in a present value worked out elsewhere: rebuild it from its inputs.

rows.label: Resource sharing within households (multiplier on an earner's gain)
rows.explainer: The site's one figure (GiveWell's): an earner's income gain is shared with the household, so it counts this many times. Read by every model that values a long-term income gain (INV-13).

rows.label: Internal validity of the effect on violence
rows.explainer: Violence is self-reported, and a drama that tells couples violence is wrong may change what women report as well as what happens. In the Uganda trial the videos worked by making disclosure seem more acceptable, which if anything raises reports, so its fall is likely real; but its binary measure of any violence wasn't in its pre-analysis plan, and the pre-registered count of incidents fell short of significance. NOVAH's pilot wasn't randomised and measured six weeks after. Our judgment 0.7, 0.3 to 1.

rows.label: External validity: a Rwandan radio drama against the studies'
rows.explainer: Place and population only (dose is in implementation_adj): the pilot was this drama in Rwanda; the Uganda trial was rural East Africa too, but videos shown at communal screenings, whose effect may have come partly through the village watching together, against radio heard at home; and its outcome is violence against any woman in the respondent's household, by anyone, not partner violence against her. Our judgment 0.85, 0.6 to 1.

rows.label: Evidence adjustment (internal and external validity), a multiplier
rows.explainer: The product of its two parts.

rows.label: Share of the outcome that wouldn't have happened anyway
rows.explainer: 1: the studies' effects are already net of their comparison villages, which had Rwanda's other violence-prevention work (RWAMREC's own programmes, community evening forums); nothing else reached these couples with the same message in 2025.

rows.label: This charity's share of the resources behind the outcome
rows.explainer: NOVAH pays its partners' in-country costs (RWAMREC, Urunana Development Communication; activity report p. 15). Unpaid help: experts and officials who reviewed the scripts, the station's promotion, advisers. Our judgment 95%, 80% to 100%.

rows.label: Share of credit used
rows.explainer: The charity's share of the resources behind the outcome; it applies whichever way credit is shared.

rows.label: Delivery adjustment
rows.explainer: 1: the effect row is already for the broadcast audience at the dose it got (most heard only some episodes, evaluation p. 9), and no study measures a dose-response by episodes (Convention 5); co-listening is in listeners_per_couple.

rows.label: Leverage and funging
rows.explainer: No funder would have paid for this drama without NOVAH; its seasons may be rebroadcast at little cost. Our judgment 1, 0.9 to 1.1.

rows.label: Years a donation waits before the charity spends it
rows.explainer: The Dutch foundation held EUR 272,751 in cash at the end of 2025 (annual accounts, p. 6), about 1.7 years of 2025's spending, much of it earmarked for the 2026 trial, when spending rises. Our judgment 1 year, 0.5 to 1.7.

rows.label: Years from the charity's spending to the intervention reaching people
rows.explainer: A season is researched, written and recorded in the months before it airs: Season 1 from September to December 2024, aired February 2025 (activity report pp. 6-7). Our judgment half a year, 0.25 to 1.

rows.label: Years from delivery to the middle of the protection
rows.explainer: The fall in violence comes over the years it lasts, so it is discounted from its middle.

rows.label: Discount for the wait until the benefits come
rows.explainer: Every wait is discounted at the shared rate, like every future benefit (the income gain's own wait is counted from delivery, in ln_income_gain_per_person).

rows.label: Counted less where the outcome isn't measured for this charity
rows.explainer: Thin: NOVAH counts its broadcast listeners in its own survey, but the effect is a judgment anchored mostly on a trial of other delivery (video screenings in Uganda); its own pilot was small, not randomised and not powered, and its 2026 trial has no published result. The shared missing-data step applies until the trial reports.

rows.label: All adjustments combined
rows.formula: evidence_adj * counterfactual_adj * attribution_share * implementation_adj * leverage_funging_adj * wait_discount * missing_data_adj
rows.explainer: The product of the adjustments above.

rows.label: Treatment costs averted, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: The site's one share for prevention programmes (@givewell_shared.treatment_costs_averted): much of the burden counted is HIV, whose lifelong treatment an infection averted saves, and injuries and depression that would be treated.

rows.label: Rebound effects, as a share of value lost
rows.explainer: 0: the malaria rebound doesn't apply.

rows.label: Investment of income increases, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: 0: no income gain is modelled.

rows.label: Other effects: children, distress, decisions, research, backlash
rows.explainer: Children who no longer see their mother beaten (in later studies, more anxiety, worse schooling and more violence as adults); the fear and pain of the violence itself and distress short of a diagnosis (GBD counts only diagnosed illness, injury and death); men who suffer violence (5.4% of married men in Rwanda, DHS); women's work lost; the pilot's other changes (women's say over money +15 points, relationship quality +0.5 SD); and what NOVAH's studies teach others making such dramas. Against them, a man who reacts against the message, or a woman told to endure (a risk NOVAH found in testing Season 2 and rewrote). Our judgment +30% of the modelled value, 0 to +80%; a side effect, weighed by the shared slider.

rows.label: Benefits and harms not modelled, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: GiveWell-style supplementary adjustments, each its own row, summed: they add to the modelled value as one share, as in GiveWell's sheets.

rows.label: Deaths averted
Value of a death averted (units of value)
rows.explainer: GiveWell's moral weights for the age band of each death averted (under five, 5–14, 15–49, 50 and over), times your multiplier on the value of a life: the site's one value of a death (docs/normalization.md 2.7).

rows.label: Units of value from deaths averted
Units of value from stillbirths averted
rows.explainer: 0: no stillbirth channel is modelled.

rows.label: Units of value from later-life income
rows.explainer: 0: no income gain is modelled.

rows.label: Units of value from illness averted
rows.explainer: A share of the deaths' and income's value, the base GiveWell's supplementary share has.

rows.label: Illness averted per couple reached, in DALYs (before adjustments)
rows.explainer: Woman-years of violence averted times the illness one causes.

rows.label: Woman-years of partner violence averted
rows.explainer: After every adjustment. For reading.

rows.label: Illness averted, in DALYs
Illness averted, in units of value
rows.explainer: The bridge from DALYs into units of value: the unit's conversion cancels it, so illness counts as healthy years whatever "Healthy year vs doubled-income year" is set to.

rows.label: Total units of value
rows.explainer: Illness and the other supplementary shares add to the modelled value side by side, as one sum of shares does in GiveWell's sheets; illness counted in DALYs comes in through its bridge, inside the side-effect share like every other outcome.

rows.label: Units of value per dollar
Salaries of the two co-directors and international subcontractors, 2025
rows.explainer: Partners' staff (RWAMREC, Urunana, IPA) are in the season lines.

rows.label: Staff pay as a share of program cost
rows.explainer: NOVAH's own share (Convention 1): {{row:staff_cost_share}}.

rows.label: Pay gap versus comparable jobs elsewhere
rows.explainer: NOVAH's co-directors design the programme, coordinate research and run partnerships, paid about EUR 33,000 to 36,500 a year each, employer costs included (May to December 2025 annualised; annual accounts, p. 8): the shared gap for research and policy staff.

rows.label: Salary forgone by staff (in-kind donation)
Share of the full cost paid by cash donations
Units of value per dollar you give
